feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
This is a strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the positioning is clear, the career progression is logical, and the experience aligns well with the headline. It reads professionally, but it would be more impactful with tighter consolidation of overlapping skills sections and more outcome-focused achievements.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level narrative: the summary, title, and progression at NACo strongly support a Digital Communications & Strategy Lead profile.  
- Good credibility and specificity: Drupal, GA4, BigQuery, Microsoft Clarity, and the 10,000+ page migration add substance and technical depth.  
- Writing is generally polished and concise, with strong action verbs and a consistent professional tone.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap significantly. Consolidating these would improve structure and save space.  
- Add sharper results: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than impact. Include measurable outcomes where possible (engagement growth, efficiency gains, campaign performance, cost savings).  
- Minor style/grammar consistency issues: add “of” in “more than 12 years of experience”; keep serial comma usage consistent (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); “French (A2/Learning)” is stylistically awkward—use “French (A2, learning)” or “Elementary (A2).” No major misspellings or typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with more specific positioning, a cleaner opening, and less overlap with the competencies section.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years’ experience” for cleaner, more modern phrasing.
- Lead with current senior value: digital strategy, platform modernization, and communications operations for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Trim channel list slightly and emphasize outcomes-oriented strengths such as governance, workflows, and translating complex policy/technical issues.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years’ experience leading web, content, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel communications, platform modernization, and the governance, workflows, and systems that enable effective digital operations at scale. Strong background in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” repeat heavily in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- Avoid adding tool names here; those are already well covered elsewhere.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening it around senior-level differentiators will make it more useful and less repetitive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, higher-value terms: “Multi-channel communications leadership” instead of “Multi-channel communication”; “Web platform governance & CMS administration” instead of “Web & CMS administration.”
- Group related items and emphasize senior scope: Digital strategy & transformation • Editorial systems & governance • Web platform modernization • Analytics & performance reporting • Cross-functional stakeholder leadership • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia & live event production
- Standardize style/plurals for parallel structure: use either all noun phrases or all “X & Y” constructions.
- Consider swapping “Workflow & systems architecture” for “Content operations & workflow design,” which is clearer and better supported by recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills and the header.
- “Digital strategy & transformation,” “analytics,” and “multimedia” already appear in Topline Skills, so avoid repeating identical wording.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear relevance, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the project footer and prior NACo entries. Tighten around scope, seniority, and 2–3 concrete outcomes or flagship initiatives.

Suggested edit:
- Open with impact + client scope: “Advise a U.S. national membership organization on digital strategy, enterprise web improvement, and cross-channel content operations.”
- Consolidate execution bullets: combine “digital systems, workflows and analytics” with governance/operating-model language to avoid sounding repetitive.
- Make the Drupal/campaign bullet outcome-led: mention launched microsites, reusable content modules, or member resource hubs if you can quantify usage, speed, or efficiency.
- Recast the AI work as a signature initiative: “Lead AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user-facing discovery experience.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item repeats details already covered in Recent Projects (AI search, microsite, anniversary campaign); keep this entry higher-level and let the project section hold specifics.
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” also echoes the 2022–2024 NACo role; emphasize consulting/advisory scope and current technical delivery.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine the strongest achievements into 4–5 bullets, led by the Drupal migration: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-based: add audience growth, engagement, open/click rates, production volume, or cost savings if available; otherwise trim “tens of thousands/thousands” language.
- Strengthen impact verbs and results: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing internal production capacity for advocacy programming, events, and recurring video content”; “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting to improve executive decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this version strategic, not operational.
- Video/programming language also appears in older NACo entries; emphasize studio build-out and organizational capacity here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Tighten it to emphasize scope, channel ownership, and operational improvements that set up the promotion.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to focus on ownership and progression: “Directed day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy messaging.”
- Combine related bullets and sharpen verbs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague phrasing with clearer impact: “Built stronger cross-team editorial planning and standardized digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Improved digital publishing workflows” overlaps with the Director role’s governance/publishing standards; keep this version tactical, not strategic.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; frame this here as scaling/formalizing the program, not originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it largely repeats the header, core competencies, and recent roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level leadership themes and sharper differentiation from the technical and analytics skills sections.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with more distinctive, outcome-oriented phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms
- Editorial governance and cross-team content operations
- Multi-channel communications leadership across web, email, social and video
- Advocacy and member-focused messaging strategy
- Audience-centered content planning and campaign storytelling
- Use “member-focused” instead of “public-sector” if targeting association/nonprofit roles; it aligns better with recent NACo and consulting work.
- Keep wording parallel: noun phrase + scope/outcome, avoiding generic labels like “leadership” alone.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” overlap heavily with Core Competencies and the header.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is broad; if kept, pair it with “campaign storytelling” to make it more specific.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill mix, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and execution themes, not repeat a software inventory.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization,” “Front-end implementation,” “Platform integrations and workflow automation,” “AI-enabled search and structured content experiences.”
- Cut lower-priority or older-signal items here, especially “jQuery,” and move niche tools like Airtable, SharePoint, and Power Pages to Technical + IT only.
- Tighten phrasing for seniority: “HTML/CSS/JavaScript implementation” reads stronger than listing languages individually.
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end web implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Structured content systems and AI-enabled search experiences”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already covered in Core Competencies.
- Most platform names duplicate the Technical + IT section; keep this section more strategic and selective.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for a senior digital leader, but it currently reads as a tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, emphasize strategic application and decision-making rather than repeating platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as outcome-oriented capabilities, e.g.: “Analytics strategy • KPI framework design • Executive dashboarding and leadership reporting • Web behavior and journey analysis • SEO and performance optimization”
- Keep only 2–3 flagship tools here, e.g.: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI/Looker Studio,” and move/remove the rest to avoid list fatigue.
- Replace “Microsoft Clarity” with a broader phrase like “behavior analytics” unless it is especially important for target roles.
- Consider adding a stronger senior-level phrase such as “measurement architecture” or “decision-support reporting.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates both “Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure” and “Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization.”
- “Leadership reporting” may overlap with executive-facing strategy already implied elsewhere; “executive dashboarding” is sharper.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Use this space to signal depth and recency, especially Drupal, which is central to recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites, governance) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- If space allows, prioritize by strength/recency: Drupal first, then WordPress/SharePoint, with Power Pages and GitHub Pages last.
- Consider adding version/scope only where meaningful, e.g., “Drupal 10” if that aligns with recent project work.
- Keep this item platform-focused; avoid adding CMS modernization or technical implementation terms already covered elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates Topline Skills: “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Consider trimming one section or making this one more specific to platform proficiency.
- “Power Pages” should be styled consistently as “Microsoft Power Pages” if used elsewhere.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more current and implementation-focused, emphasizing tools you’ve actively used in recent roles/projects.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End Development & Technical Implementation
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- If accurate, add scope/context instead of only tools: Front-end implementation for Drupal/WordPress, API-based integrations, tag management, edge scripting, and deployment automation
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required; they add little value for a senior candidate

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with Topline Skills: “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery • API integrations.” Keep one version shorter or make this section more tool-specific.
- “Cloudflare Workers” and “GitHub Actions” are useful differentiators; keep them, as they add more uniqueness than the core coding terms.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow automation capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize systems-building, not just PM/chat tools: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira/Asana/Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams”
- Remove weaker or older-feeling tools unless they are current and used recently; Basecamp is the easiest cut.
- If space allows, add a short qualifier for impact: “workflow automation, intake tracking, approvals, and cross-team coordination”
- Consider renaming the heading to “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems” to better match the actual mix of tools.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating them elsewhere without added specificity.
- Jira, Asana, Trello, Slack, and Teams are common tools; keep only those most relevant to recent roles.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this item is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses the scale of your email leadership. It should signal enterprise email/engagement capability, not just list platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Enterprise newsletter operations • Audience segmentation • Campaign deployment**
- If accurate, strengthen with scope: **Platforms supporting newsletters and member communications reaching tens of thousands of stakeholders**
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; lead with the most current/enterprise-grade tool.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Engagement” is already implied in Core Competencies and work history; avoid adding generic phrases like “multi-channel communications.”
- Don’t repeat analytics or automation terms here; those are already covered in separate Technical + IT categories.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and reads as setup work rather than concrete contribution. Since this is an older role, keep it concise and emphasize foundational impact without repeating later NACo leadership achievements.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground progression and scope: “Promoted across two digital media roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Tighten the second sentence around 2–3 concrete contributions: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and improved day-to-day publishing workflows.”
- Replace “high-impact” with specifics if available: add volume, audience, cadence, or event scale (e.g., number of livestreams, weekly series length, traffic/email reach).
- Clarify supervision modestly: use “provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” only if people guidance matters for the promotion story.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; differentiate this as launching or early production support.
- Avoid repeating broad workflow/governance language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes/ownership so it adds distinct value without repeating later digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize initiative and scope: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the podcast the lead achievement: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- Trim generic phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with a clearer contribution such as “produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes launched, audience growth, internal stakeholders supported, or projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item focused on innovation/research support plus the podcast launch.
- Avoid overstating team leadership here, since stronger leadership evidence appears in later NACo roles.
